title: Jamaica's Call Center Jobs Fall by a Third: AI, Costs and the Pivot | Across the Water, Ep. 9
lede: Jamaica's outsourcing sector, the call centers and back offices that work for overseas clients, has fallen from about 60,000 jobs to about 40,000 by the industry's count (50,000 by the government's). On Oct. 30 the Bank of Jamaica's governor said the business is vulnerable to AI and its owners must pivot. Industry leaders say AI is not the cause. This episode explains the size of the sector, the two job counts, the four explanations for the decline and the plan to move up the value chain.
keyPoints: Industry count: about 40,000 outsourcing jobs, down from a peak of about 60,000; government count: 50,000 in March 2026, from 62,000 in March 2024 (GSAJ; Form 18-K via Jamaica Observer).
The sector spent an estimated US$780 million in Jamaica in the year to March 2026, down from about US$1 billion; bauxite and alumina exports earned US$612 million in 2025 (Jamaica Observer).
Bank of Jamaica governor Brian Langrin (Oct 30): the business is vulnerable to AI and "it has to be the entrepreneurs that pivot" (Gleaner).

GSAJ's Yoni Epstein says no Jamaican outsourcing job has been lost to AI and blames productivity, talent and Hurricane Melissa; Opposition spokesman Peter Bunting warns AI threatens the sector (Jamaica Observer).
A government working group aims to shift the job mix from 80:20 outsourcing-to-knowledge work to 60:40 (Jamaica Observer).
